name: Museum der Völker Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum der Völker in Schwaz: Western Austria's unique ethnographic museum featuring masterpieces of African and Asian tribal art.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Museum der Völker is situated on the sunny slopes above the historic silver town of Schwaz in the Tyrolean Unterinntal (Silberregion Karwendel) at an altitude of approximately 560 meters. Founded in 1995 by Tyrolean photographer, globetrotter, and journalist Gert Chesi, it stands as the only independent ethnographic museum in Western Austria. Following extensive renovation and new construction in 2013, the museum presents itself as a cutting-edge, light-flooded cultural center that builds bridges between continents and fosters dialogue among world cultures, global religions, and contemporary art.

Route & Requirements

The spectacular permanent exhibition comprises over 1,000 exquisite ethnographic exhibits, ritual masterpieces, and sacred objects from Africa and Asia. Undisputed highlights include the outstanding Asian Collection with centuries-old Buddha sculptures from Thailand, Burma, and Cambodia, ornately decorated terracotta pieces from the Chinese Han and Tang dynasties, and rare ancestral figures from Indonesia. The African Department captivates visitors with expressive ritual masks, ancestor statues, and cult objects of West African peoples (including the Yoruba, Dogon, and Fon), as well as fascinating artifacts of the animist Vodun tradition in Benin and Togo. Alongside the permanent exhibition, the museum curates high-profile temporary exhibitions illuminating contemporary global issues, photographic art, postcolonial debates, and indigenous ways of life. An idyllic sculpture garden invites quiet contemplation after your tour.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum der Völker in Schwaz is open year-round from Thursday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Monday to Wednesday; special group openings on request). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €9.00, seniors and students approx. €7.50, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €4.00, children under 6 free; affordable family tickets available for approx. €20.00. Holders of the Silberregion Karwendel regional guest card receive discounts. Getting there by car: Via the Inntal Autobahn A12 (Schwaz exit), proceed along the B171 into the town center and follow signage to St.-Martin-Straße 16; free parking is available right at the museum. By public transport: ÖBB trains to Schwaz station, from where the Schwaz city bus runs directly to the Museum der Völker or St. Martin stop.

Tips

The entire museum building is barrier-free and fully accessible for wheelchair users and strollers via ramps and modern elevators. Take advantage of the on-site audio guide or book a guided tour to gain deeper insights into the ritual significance of the ancestral sculptures. Combine your visit with a scenic walk to nearby Freundsberg Castle or into the historic town center of Schwaz.
